newsitem.title: UK: Uk drugs shares weaker as investors take profits.
newsitem.headline: Uk drugs shares weaker as investors take profits.

text.p: Shares in British pharmaceutical companies fell on Thursday, hit by a weak overnight performance by drugs shares in New York and profit taking after a strong run, dealers said.
Glaxo Wellcome was down 40p, or 2.79 percent, at 13.60 stg at 0948 GMT, making it the biggest percentage loser in the FTSE 100 index.
SmithKline Beecham Plc fell 25p or 2.01 percent to 12.21-1/2 stg and Zeneca dropped 42-1/2p to 22.22-1/2 stg, a fall of 1.88 percent.
"It's the same story for all the big drugs shares," one market-maker said. "The sector was weak in New York and after a very good run some people are taking profits."

The pharmaceuticals sector has been among the strongest sectors in Britain's stock market over the past year. Along with financial shares, the sector has been one of the main engines driving the FTSE 100 index to a succession of record highs.
